title: The procedural survey tank is deleted; a hull is MÖRK or it is nothing
context: Playing the live V1 build the owner saw the wrong hull on load: "Main now loaded the ancient model for the tank. On refresh it swapped to the correct one, but there is still a frame where the old tank loads and is then replaced. REMOVE that model from the UNITS, remove it from everywhere." The relic was not an asset at all, which is why no lock file named it: it was makeTank() in src/units.js, a ~350-triangle Lambert casting with treads, a 3x3 sphere shell rack and two mini-guns, described in the source as the mesh-unit proof of concept. It was still live in four places: UNITS.tank (a roster entry the Units lab listed as 'the procedural tank', with its own codex page LORE.tank, SURVEY TANK, PATTERN A), the synchronous fallback inside UNITS.mork / mork-low / mork-proxy (built with userData.loading while the GLB downloaded and swapped out by applyCreature, which is the frame the owner saw), the swarm lab's opening hull, and buildUnit's default for an unknown name.
outcome: makeTank and its 79-line block are gone from src/units.js, together with the UNITS.tank roster entry, the unitcatalog 'tank' choice and the LORE.tank codex page. In its place makePendingHull() returns an EMPTY Group carrying MORK_UNIT (asset 'mork', baseScale, lift) plus loading: true: the unit contract with no body, so every consumer sizes, places and reports it exactly as the hull it stands in for and it draws nothing. The three MÖRK tiers return it until their bytes land; buildUnit's default for an unknown name is now UNITS[DEFAULT_TANK]. The swarm lab stands the placeholder in its lane and swaps MÖRK in when ready instead of building the casting. td-tab's briefing-card icon builds DEFAULT_TANK rather than the literal 'tank'. Nothing non-MÖRK can be drawn any more, because the code that drew it no longer exists. Kept deliberately: the metal lab's SUBJECTS key 'tank' (a ?unit=tank deep-link key whose cast is already buildCreature(DEFAULT_TANK), labelled 'MÖRK (full)'), td-tab's spriteShot cache key 'tank', the 'tank' kill-source, bloom-group and audio-bus names, and glbmodels' makeShellRack / makeHeatSleeve / addGunTubes, which are shape helpers for authored models rather than the relic.
alternatives: Keep the casting and hide it for a frame: rejected, because a hidden relic is still a relic in the roster, the codex and the Units lab, which is what the owner asked to remove.

Return null until MÖRK is ready: rejected, because playerMesh is dereferenced unconditionally in dozens of td-tab paths (scale, bloom groups, placeActors, feel), so a null hull is a far larger and riskier change than a meshless one.

Delete a model file under assets/: not applicable. The relic was procedural code. No GLB, no docs/*.lock.json entry, no scripts/assets.mjs lock and no ATTRIBUTIONS.md credit ever existed for it, so there was nothing to remove there.
evidence: artifacts/qa/legacy-hull.mjs through scripts/browser-lock.sh: a census of every Object3D subtree entering the scene, taken by patching Object3D.prototype.add on the vendored three module at document start (hook installed 124 ms, first hull 1291 ms). Over the story boot (world=story&stage=7) four hull subtrees entered: three empty placeholders (asset 'mork', loading, 0 meshes) and then MÖRK at 1574 ms (50 meshes, HOVER_RIG, TURRET_YAW, Long_cannon_barrel). No subtree carried userData.ammoDots, the deleted casting's shell rack, and no hull carried a Lambert material. Raw census artifacts/qa/legacy-hull/census-story.json, verdict census-verdict.json, screenshot story-tank-rollout.png.

The same probe re-ran the Units evidence: units-tier-mork 24196/50, units-tier-mork-low 6742/49, units-tier-mork-proxy 1706/1 with its proxy flag; units-dart-quiver and units-dart-heptapod firing MISSILE_MOTION; ?unit=tank selecting nothing; entriesIn('friendly') carrying no 'tank'.

node scripts/browser-test.mjs --defense green (11 steps). --story-world reached story-world-rotor-kill green and then failed on the Rotor heat-peak step (window.__rotorHeatMax 0.037 against > 0.05): a timing-sensitive step the test itself documents as racing the Quiver hand-over, and recorded as flaky on main. Nothing in this change touches tower heat or the sentry pilot; it was NOT re-run, because the session's browser-run budget was spent.
npm test (120 test programs), npm run check (architecture guard included) and npm run assets:check green.
src/td-tab.js 13506 -> 13505 lines; docs/architecture-budget.json lowered to match. topLevelModules unchanged: no top-level module was deleted.
